items.subject: Module Builder - Phase 1: Create and use modules in Edge Studio
items.story: An operator can create or import a module, test/package it and activate it locally without a core release, CLI or hosted-library account.
criteria: Hardware-agent, device/setup and workflow contributions use versioned dynamic contracts and real installed packages.
Existing default capabilities are uninstallable/restorable through a real local demo-library lifecycle without losing configuration/history.
The app provides editing, templates, schema-driven preview, tests/logs, validation, packaging, import/export and explicit activation.
Code generation happens in the user's own AI harness using a module-builder-skill; no module CLI or built-in AI generator.
Before install/update/activation, prompt for app-wide device/log exports and demonstrate user-directed restoration of managed state.
A new physical sensor and workflow block can be authored and installed on another Pi without core-source edits.
Full privileged host execution is intentional; supervision is not a sandbox and arbitrary host changes are not universally reversible.

items.subject: Module Builder - Phase 2: Share and sell modules in the online library
items.story: Independent authors publish inspectable modules, users discover and buy them, and contributors receive payment while installed versions remain usable offline.
criteria: Self-service publishing includes publisher identities, immutable releases, inspectable source, compatibility metadata and official delivery.
Automated acceptance checks precede publication; initial human spam/content moderation follows publication, with community management as the end goal.
Ratings, rating-count-weighted builder aggregates, download counts and community inspection reports are available without safety-certification claims.
Commerce is REQUIRED in this phase: checkout, contributor payouts, refunds, purchase records and offline entitlements are implemented and tested.
Installed paid versions continue offline without a continuous license-server dependency; external module services may still need connectivity.
Licensing/fork rights remain open; do not promise strong anti-copy enforcement or mandatory restrictive redistribution.
Web-library operational ownership is separate from community module creation; monitoring/backup/report/removal mechanisms are established.

items.subject: Back up Edge Studio and restore it if a module causes problems
items.story: As an operator I can export managed device state and diagnostic logs, then restore through the app-wide recovery path when an extension change fails.
criteria: Define backup coverage for configuration, workflows, module releases/artifacts/state, retained history/media and required credential/node/wallet integration.
Export device is restorable managed state; Export logs is diagnostic. Neither is confused with a credential-free shareable module package.
Protect credentials according to the app-wide backup policy and document a recovery route if the app must first be repaired/reinstalled.
Test export/restore on an app-approved Pi baseline, including failed extension updates and compatible code/state restoration.
Integrate with existing app-wide export/log work; do not build a second module-only backup system or promise full OS/firmware rollback.

items.subject: Define what modules can add and how they work with Edge Studio
items.story: As an author I have documented hardware/device/workflow contracts so a compatible package can add a type without core code changes.
criteria: Inventory every current capability/block/template and assign package ownership and observable parity checks.
Define namespaced manifest identity/version, runtime entry points, contributions, dependencies, compatibility and declared host access.
Define lifecycle/error/cancellation/events and generic UI schemas for forms, guides and wizard steps.
Platform/runtimes/architectures inherit Edge Studio app policy; per-module requirements are declared and checked.
Define legacy IDs/state migration boundaries and keep the module manager usable with no packages installed.

items.subject: Install, update and remove modules, starting with a working example
items.story: As an operator I can uninstall and genuinely download/reinstall an existing capability through one complete local lifecycle.
criteria: Persist immutable installed releases, drafts, activation/configuration state and package integrity/compatibility results.
Import/inspection does not execute code; show access and the backup prompt before executable hooks.
Extract HTTP JSON Source/Fetch and use a separate local demo catalog with real downloadable bytes, not a shared-directory copy.
Demonstrate uninstall, missing-module placeholders, real download, inactive installation, explicit activation, restart persistence and retained history/configuration.
Keep updates manual and failed-install/reinstall states actionable; record backup/export integration as dependent on F0.

items.subject: Add hardware support by installing modules
items.story: As an author I can add a privileged hardware capability without adding a hard-coded agent branch.
criteria: Convert the fixed host-agent dispatcher into a module-aware supervisor and capability registry.
Package camera/GPIO/I2C/local-MQTT behavior, prerequisites and lifecycle operations with explicit ownership.
Support full privileged host entry points, durable progress, health/cancellation and clear partial-failure/reboot reporting.
Setup is repeatable; uninstall handles shared dependencies and reports host changes that remain.
Verify representative physical Pi hardware behavior; do not describe root execution as sandboxed.

items.subject: Add device choices and setup guides through modules
items.story: As an operator I can configure new contributed device types through the existing Devices experience.
criteria: Replace hard-coded device choices/forms/guides with registry-driven, schema-defined fields, defaults and wizard steps.
Dispatch backend configuration/reads/events/captures through registered providers.
Preserve existing IDs, credentials, device configuration, capture hashing and event lifecycle behavior.
Missing/disabled packages retain configured devices and show actionable unavailable states.
Arbitrary custom views/editors are deferred until a concrete required example demonstrates the need.

items.subject: Add new workflow steps through modules
items.story: As an author I can contribute workflow blocks and handlers without editing core type unions or execution branches.
criteria: Replace compiled block lists, configuration/help/summaries and dispatch with registered descriptors and handlers.
Use explicit start/data/action roles; preserve scheduling, cancellation, run/block history and structured errors.
Preserve existing media/hash/proof semantics and application-service budgets for ordinary calls; privileged code is not constrained by those policies.
Pin resolved package versions for execution and retain placeholders/history for unavailable blocks.
Handle uncertain side effects without automatically repeating payments after timeouts.

items.subject: Turn built-in features into modules users can remove and reinstall
items.story: As an existing user I retain my working devices/workflows while built-in capabilities become removable packages.
criteria: Assign every existing choice a final package owner; remove temporary migration adapters and permanent hidden built-in fallbacks.
Migrate legacy IDs/configuration without recreating devices or losing histories/secrets.
For each package verify disable/remove, unavailable states, actual local-library download, inactive install, activation and restored behavior.
Verify reboot, interrupted hooks, shared hardware/dependencies, offline use, zero-extension operation and restoration of the default set.
Removed defaults do not silently reinstall on ordinary app restart/update; purge is a separate explicit action.

items.subject: Create, edit and test modules inside Edge Studio
items.story: As a creator I edit and preview module files in Edge Studio and test behavior before explicit local activation.
criteria: Provide My Modules, local drafts, template selection, file/code editing and schema-defined configuration/setup previews.
Expose supported test fixtures/development runs, logs and clear failure results; distinguish preview from actual privileged execution.
Separate drafts from prepared immutable releases; edits invalidate preparation status.
Integrate app-wide backup prompts before install/update/local activation and preserve configuration/history on removal.
No module CLI, full IDE or in-app AI generation harness is required; publishing is Phase 2.

items.subject: Help creators build modules and prove they work on another Pi
items.story: As a creator I generate source in my own AI harness with the module-builder-skill, then package and share it through the app.
criteria: Publish a skill/reference hand-off covering actual manifest/runtime contracts, schemas, examples and test/package requirements.
Support source import, validation, target-aware artifact preparation, source/package export and import on another instance.
No hosted account/publication is required for local activation or direct sharing; exclude device instances/credentials from shareable artifacts.
An independent contributor creates a new physical sensor capability and workflow block, tests on a Pi and installs on a second instance without core edits.
Generated code is not presumed safe or correct; show execution trust and test limitations accurately.

items.subject: Give creators accounts and store published module versions
items.story: As a contributor I own a stable publisher identity and publish versioned artifacts/source through a centrally hosted service.
criteria: Provide publisher accounts/namespaces, scoped publishing credentials and release ownership.
Store immutable artifacts and the matching source snapshot/manifest/dependency/access metadata.
Provide integrity/provenance verification without claiming code-safety certification or DRM.
Establish service monitoring, backups, recovery and named operational ownership separate from community module creation.

items.subject: Find modules online and add them to Edge Studio
items.story: As an operator I find compatible capabilities in the library and install official releases through Edge Studio.
criteria: Provide searchable/filterable module pages, publisher profiles, versions, docs and compatibility/access information.
Connect the app to actual hosted package downloads using the Phase 1 package model.
Retain backup prompts, inactive installation and explicit activation; preserve installed versions when the library is offline.
Support both free and paid listings; paid entitlement enforcement in the official delivery path integrates with F15.

items.subject: Check uploads automatically and handle spam after publication
items.story: As an author I publish after automated checks without a human approval gate, while the library can address spam and inappropriate content.
criteria: Define and implement deterministic acceptance checks for package/manifest/metadata/artifact integrity and compatibility declarations.
Publication is self-service once checks pass; no mandatory manual code review or approval before publication.
Initially support human post-publication spam/content moderation, reporting, removals/appeals and an audit trail.
Document the path to community-managed moderation and name initial owners/transition criteria.
AI-assisted checks remain an evaluation option, not a mandatory dependency, automatic safety badge or claimed completed scan.

items.subject: Let users inspect module code and report problems
items.story: As a community member I inspect the exact release source before purchase/download and report concerns about that version.
criteria: Expose source, manifest, dependencies, requested privileges and release differences tied to the actual delivered artifact.
Keep published snapshots immutable while allowing labelled local modifications and separately versioned releases.
Support version-specific inspection reports distinct from ratings and purchase reviews.
Do not select a restrictive redistribution license or certify safety merely from public source, signatures or community reports.

items.subject: Show module ratings, creator ratings and download numbers
items.story: As a user I compare community experience and popularity without mistaking them for a safety guarantee.
criteria: Provide server-side 1-5 star ratings with counts and one replaceable rating per account/module.
Compute builder aggregates from all individual module ratings weighted by rating count; unrated modules do not lower averages.
Define successful-download counting and abuse controls; keep totals visible for installed modules.
Provide rating/download sorting and clearly distinguish verified purchases from other community feedback.
No rating, verified identity or download figure is represented as code-safety certification.

items.subject: Let users buy modules, pay creators and receive refunds
items.story: As a contributor I sell official module releases and receive payment; buyers have clear purchase and refund records.
criteria: Commerce is required for Phase 2 completion; implement checkout with one selected payment provider.
Persist authoritative order/payment records and handle asynchronous provider events idempotently.
Implement contributor onboarding/payout and refund paths with auditable reconciliation and purchase-support states.
Agree pricing/purchase/update/refund/payout terms before launch; subscriptions are not assumed as baseline.
Allow source inspection before purchase and preserve the openness/anti-copy limitations recorded in D8.

items.subject: Keep purchased modules working when the library is offline
items.story: As a buyer I install my purchased official release and keep using it offline without continuous license-server access.
criteria: Bind official download/install access to authoritative purchase records and version/update rights.
Define and verify offline receipts/entitlements with a tested key/lifecycle model; signatures prove provenance, not copy protection.
Test purchase, install, restart and installed-version use while the hosted library is unavailable.
Handle refunds/revocation/update eligibility according to agreed terms without silently assuming always-online checks or remote disablement.
Recognize that full host control/source editing permits bypassing local checks; no strong DRM or restrictive redistribution enforcement is promised.
